When and why did you start training for fighting? I first began training when I was 14, mainly for the fact it was the only sport I didn’t get kicked out of. It was a way for me to work out some of my anger and next thing I knew I turned pro when I was 16 and I found my calling in life.

What ranks and titles have you held? Former UFC middleweight champion, King of the Cage middleweight belt, black belt in BJJ

What fight do you consider the key fight in your career? The Usman fight. That was the fight that I learned jiu jitsu doesn’t work and you need to get up. 

Who is your favorite fighter and why? I don’t have a favorite fighter, but I respect the old-school fighters the most. People who showed up, fought hard, and didn’t make excuses.

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? Not really heroes. I respect people who’ve been through real adversity and didn’t let it break them. Anyone who takes responsibility for their life and keeps moving forward has my respect.

What are your current ranks in martial arts? Black Belt in BJJ

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? I just want to give back to my fans. They have allowed me to make a life out of this sport. Without them I would probably be in prison somewhere. 

Beyond a championship and money, what motivates you? Besides money, my motivation to fight is for my fans. They are the reason I get to train every day and still pay my bills. 

What was your job before you started fighting? I turned pro when I was 16. I’ve always been a fighter.

Favorite Striking technique: Not getting punched in the face technique

What is one thing you want UFC fans to know about you? What you see is what you get. I’m not playing a character. I fight hard, I speak honestly, and I show up every time.

What does it mean for you to fight for the UFC? Fighting in the UFC of course is a massive milestone for me. I’ve worked for the last 10 years sharpening my skills and gaining the experience I need to not just be here but to thrive here. 

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training when I was 15 years old. I began training from being inspired by watching the UFC. At the time I was a very insecure and shy kid. I felt that everything it took to be a successful fighter were qualities that I did not have growing up — confidence, discipline, belief and security. I wanted to be a champion in this sport from that moment, not because I wanted money or fame, but because I wanted all the mental, physical and emotional attributes that came with it.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? My favorite fighter is Georges St-Pierre. He was a complete martial artist who was able to win and finish opponents in every facet of the sport. His completeness and intelligence towards the game is something I don’t think we’ve seen from any fighter since.

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? My hero is my father. Somebody who led by example working extremely hard and being the most supportive and generous person I know. He is my idol and my greatest supporter. 

What are your current ranks in martial arts? BJJ Brown Belt under Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani and Nick Bohli 

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Three-time A1 Combat Featherweight Champion 

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why? My 2nd pro fight I fought an incredibly talented prospect from Uriah Faber’s gym. A 6’2” Dagestani who was a great grappler and striker. In the fight he eye poked me in the first round for which I took all 5 minutes to recover from. My vision never returned in that eye, however I decided to continue fighting anyway. He then swarmed me and hit me with a left hook that broke my orbital bone on my OTHER eye , which caused swelling that gave me double vision. So I fought essentially 12 minutes of that fight with no vision. Double vision in both eyes. I fought through that, ended up dropping him very badly in the last minute of the fight which he barely recovered from. I ended up winning the fight by decision.

Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you? What motivates me is that through being a great martial artist and fighter I will become a greater person. Nothing requires more out of me than this sport.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to college at the University of Oregon but dropped out after my first year to pursue fighting more seriously.

What was your job before you started fighting? I was working as a barista earlier in my career. I’d work 4 am to11 am every day at a coffee shop so I could still get my two training sessions in. 

Favorite grappling technique: Back take 

Favorite Striking technique: Question mark kick 

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: My significant other is Bianca Lebosnoyani, who is the sister of my teammate Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani. We have been together over four years and she has supported me throughout my entire Amateur and Professional Career. No specific hobbies outside of fighting. Training is my life and my only real passion other than my family and friends.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started fighting Muay Thai when I was nine. My brothers used to do it and they used to win medals and I wanted some of that. First session I done, I fell in love with it. I grew up in an estate in London, which isn’t the best and it’s easy to get side-tracked. So my parents put me and my siblings into sport at a young age to keep us distracted and surrounded by positive role models. 

What professional titles have you held? Was ranked number 1 in the UK for Muay  Thai

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? I won 35 amateur belts in Muay Thai, including five world titles and multiple European titles. I was UK number one in amateur. 

Any belts/ranks in grappling disciplines? Purple belt in BJJ. Fought on Polaris and got Sub of the Night. 

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? My last fight, as she hit hard and was a bit too big for me, so I made the decision to go back down to my actual weight class this fight. I made the fight harder for myself, as I went to war when I should’ve just played it smart and easy like I did in the first round. But we live and learn. I had fun. 

Who is your favorite fighter and why? My favorite fighter is Israel Adesanya. I love how he changed striking in MMA, and how he utilizes fakes and set ups and distance control in his fights. Also, I love anime, too, and I’m from the same country, Nigeria. 

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I didn’t go to college. Took a gap year and ended up being a full-time fighter. 

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked at a sports shop at 16. Then did the tickets at football stadiums part time. Thats it. Then became a full time fighter. 

Origin of nickname: Someone who I was really close to, thought of as an older brother, at the start of my MMA journey had the name nightmare. He was a really high-level domestic fighter: Jahreau Shepherd. Unfortunately, he got murdered at his 30th birthday party, one that I attended, five years ago. We had the same dream to become UFC world champion. He didn’t get to fulfil that. But I can now for the both of us by carrying his name on. 

Personal Life / Background: I have 5 siblings: 2 brothers. 3 sisters. All 8 years apart in age. I live with my nan. I have a big extended family and they are all supportive in what I’m doing. 

Who are 3 people you'd love to meet or work with? Ronaldo. Israel Adesanya. Mr Beast. 

What are your hobbies, activities or other interests when not training for a fight? I love anime and manga. I spend a lot of my time watching, reading or sometimes drawing it. Sometimes I try to emulate fight scenes in my fight and it gets me all fired up. I cosplay sometimes too. I used to love football, but my team Manchester United is doing really bad so I tapered down in watching it. I still watch the national games and follow it slightly. I like playing football, too, with my sisters; they do it semi-pro. I love traveling, seeing new cultures and learning new stuff. New experiences. I love sleeping.
